title: Day 9 of my paper-trading bot competition: I made a mistake that kept Charles from switching to his better morning pick, and here's what the accounts would have had without it
author: DadsGamesandCharles
selftext:
Quick recap for anyone new: over the past year I've built a bunch of AI trading bots, and on Oct 22 I started a public paper-money competition with accounts at $5,000 each. It started with 13 accounts, and I've since retired my own hand-traded account, so 12 are left: 10 strategies, an account that follows Charles 2.0, which is a prediction engine that posts its up-picks before the open, and an AI agent's account called Brokgot. This is the day 9 update, covering everything through the Nov 3 close.



Everything below is paper money. Nobody steps in to fix the accounts.



My mistake, and what it cost



I'm putting this right up front because it matters more than anything else in this update. On Oct 28 I made a change to Charles 2.0's code that stopped him from swapping to a better pick in the morning once he had lined up a pick the afternoon before. That was wrong. I didn't even realize I'd done it as it was just something that Cursor brought up and during the course of a converation somehow added it in. Either way, Charles is supposed to be able to take another look before the open and switch to his morning pick if he likes it better. My change was in place for four sessions: Oct 29, Oct 30, Nov 2 and Nov 3. During those days the accounts were stuck with the afternoon pick even when Charles's morning list said something else.  


I've fixed it, and starting with the next session Charles can switch to his morning pick again. He can change his mind before the open, and once the market opens he sticks with that pick.

Most of that gap came from two days. On Monday, Nov 2, most of the accounts bought AGX, which slid all day, when Charles's morning list would have had them in a different stock that ended up roughly flat. That one swap is most of the gap for the strategies, including nearly all of Strategy 2's. Strategy 3 and Strategy 7 got out of AGX early that morning, so Monday cost them a lot less, and that's why their gaps are small. On Tuesday, Nov 3, the accounts held FUN, which sank after the open, when Charles's morning pick was MSTR, which ran up after the open. That's where nearly all of the gap comes from for Charles 2.0 and Strategy 1, which weren't in AGX on Monday. For most of the other strategies Tuesday changes less than you'd think, because they would have ended up in FUN later in the day anyway and taken much of the same hit. Oct 29 made only a small difference, and Oct 30 came out about the same either way, so I didn't count it.



To be clear, the would-have-had numbers are estimates of what would have happened, worked out from minute-by-minute prices, not real trades. The has-now numbers are the real paper account balances, and those are what every other number in this post is based on. Still, it was my mistake, it's fixed, and I'd rather tell you than have you find it.

  
One small note on those estimates: Strategy 3 and Strategy 7 each sold AGX a little lower on Monday than the minute prices show, so their would-have-had numbers are probably each about $80 too low.

Brokgot was back in action today, betting against two stocks a few minutes after the open. RSI went the wrong way almost right away, and Brokgot was out of it by 9:38 AM for a $193.16 loss. RSI kept climbing and closed more than 5% above its open, so getting out early saved it from a much bigger hit. The JD bet worked: JD opened at its high for the day and drifted lower, and Brokgot held it until 3:50 PM for a $55.40 gain. That left it down $137.76 on the day.



SPY for comparison



SPY, close to close: Oct 22 -1.18%, Oct 23 -0.52%, Oct 26 +0.71%, Oct 27 +0.56%, Oct 28 +0.34%, Oct 29 -0.38%, Oct 30 -1.77%, Nov 2 -0.48%, Nov 3 +0.30%. From the Oct 21 close to the Nov 3 close, SPY is down about 2.42%. Over the same stretch the 10 strategies combined are down 14.07% in paper dollars, and the 10 strategies plus Charles 2.0 are down 13.79%.



Being straight with you: the bots are now well behind SPY, by more than 11 points. The first six days had them comfortably ahead, and the last three wiped that out and then some. That's a real gap and I'm not going to dress it up.



Today, Nov 3: another red day



SPY was up 0.30%, but the 10 strategies combined lost $5,228.70 and every one of them finished red. Strategy 3 (-$100.61) and Strategy 8 (-$159.05) held up best and Strategy 3 moved up to second overall. Strategy 9 lost $587.04 but is still the only account in the green, at +8.45%. Charles 2.0 lost $625.25.



It was all one stock: FUN. It popped about 1.7% in the very first minute and then slid the rest of the day, closing 3.68% below its open. The accounts got in during the first few minutes, mostly after that pop, and most of them held it into the afternoon. Strategy 3 and Strategy 8 lost far less on it than the others. It didn't have to start that way: Charles's morning pick was MSTR, which ran up after the open, but because of my Oct 28 change the accounts were stuck with FUN from the afternoon before. For Charles 2.0's own account, today is the day that mistake hurt the most.

How Charles 2.0's picks did today



There were four picks today. For each one I checked whether the stock's high for the day, between the 9:30 AM open and 3:59 PM, reached +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0% above the 9:30 AM open, using minute bars.



1. MSTR: high +5.26% above the open. Touched all three levels.

2. FUN: high +1.68% above the open. Touched all three levels, but only in the first minute.

3. BLKB: high +1.81% above the open. Touched all three levels.

4. SG: high +0.61% above the open. Touched +0.25% and +0.5%, but not +1.0%.



So all four touched +0.25% and +0.5%, and three of four touched +1.0%. MSTR was the standout, running more than 5% above the open by late morning. MSTR was Charles's top pick this morning, and it's the stock the accounts would have started the day in if my Oct 28 change hadn't kept them on FUN. FUN is the flip side: it did touch the levels, but only right at the open, before the accounts were in.



Running tally for live Charles 2.0 picks, Sep 22 through Nov 3 (31 sessions, 124 picks): 108 touched +0.25% above the open (87%), 99 touched +0.5% (80%), and 80 touched +1.0% (65%). What I care about is whether a pick reaches those levels during the day, since I want the money that same day, not the next.



Keeping it honest



Nine sessions is still a short stretch, and the last three have been rough, so the doubts some people have had look a lot more reasonable tonight. Mistakes happen. That's exactly why this is happening in public, red days and my own mistakes included. I'd much rather find these problems now on paper than later with real money.



A few people asked about the strategy: I'm keeping the exact rules to myself, but the bots all start from the same morning picks and differ in how they get in and out.



What's next



Charles is back to using his morning pick starting with the next session. He can switch before the open, and after the open he sticks with it. The next few sessions should show how that plays out. Daily results after each close, and a fuller write-up as the sample grows. See you tomorrow.



Questions you probably have



Is this real money? No. Every account is paper money.



Is paper trading realistic? Not entirely. Paper can't show market impact, and real fills are usually worse. That's the main reason my early backtests got cut down.



Will you ever trade real money? Yes, we will.



Can I buy or subscribe to anything? Not yet.



Is this financial advice? No. The picks are research ideas to watch, not tips, and nothing here is a guarantee of anything.



Are AI agents involved? Yes. AI agents help build, test and run the bots, and one of the accounts is traded by an AI agent. I'm the one who reviews and posts this.



Why publish bad numbers? Because a track record that only shows the good days isn't worth much.



What if a bot loses? Then it loses in public. The accounts are paper and no one steps in to fix them.



Why did the competition start on Oct 22? Earlier starts on Monday and Tuesday had account setup problems, so those days don't count.



Where can I follow along? On this profile. I'll post daily results here after the close.



Have a question that isn't here? Ask in the comments and I'll answer it.



Paper money only. Not financial advice. Written with help from AI.

comments.body: The separation between the paper balances and the reconstructed 'would-have' balances is useful. I'd add a regression test with an afternoon pick A and a better morning pick B, asserting the switch before the open and no switch after it. Keeping the fix's version and start date beside the forward results would make it easier to judge the corrected system without blending hindsight estimates into its track record.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
Yeah, the test you’re referring to is actually what was nagging me and why knew something was wrong before I checked it.

I don’t really need to run any more tests on these things as the one that actually matters is the one that’s running right now, even if there was a hiccup in it. I caught it because Charles never behaves the way that he behaved the past few days and because I’m so familiar with him and how he operates I just knew something was wrong.
